resources.string: Loading apps; the firewall will not be enabled automatically
Apply your changes first, or press Back to discard them. The advanced interface retains the upstream features.
↑↓ Select an app · OK changes its policy · Apply rules to activate changes
Core UIDs are protected; apps sharing a UID share a policy. LAN includes private ranges and discovery traffic. New apps follow the advanced mode default.
This UID is used by Android or maintenance services and cannot be blocked in the TV interface. Do not block the entire system UID 1000 to restrict one service.

Unrestricted: no additional app restriction.
LAN only: allows the AFWall+ LAN and discovery rules while blocking Wi-Fi/Ethernet internet, mobile data, and VPN traffic.
Blocked: denies direct LAN/WAN traffic, subject to the engine’s loopback, DNS, and system-proxy exceptions.
Apps sharing a UID share a policy. Root-capable software can change firewall rules.
Apply rules and enable the firewall?

Grant this app root access in Magisk or your root manager. Rules are applied by the AFWall+ engine for IPv4 and IPv6.\n\nStart with one nonessential app. Core UIDs stay allowed, and the advanced allowlist/blocklist mode is preserved. Do not enable upstream AFWall+ or another firewall manager at the same time. Boot restoration follows upstream behavior.
\n\nSaved scripts or active advanced rules are configured. They are preserved and processed by the upstream engine and may override the three policies. Cancel and inspect Advanced if needed.
